Built-in defaults\n6\t2. Global config file (`~/.config/needle/config.yaml`)\n7\t3. Workspace config file (`.needle.yaml` in workspace root)\n8\t4. Environment variables (`NEEDLE_*` prefix)\n9\t5. CLI arguments\n10\t\n11\tThis guide covers the most commonly used configuration options.\n12\t\n13\t---\n14\t\n15\t## Worker Configuration\n16\t\n17\tThe `worker` section controls fleet behavior and worker spawning.\n18\t\n19\t### Basic Worker Settings\n20\t\n21\t```yaml\n22\t# ~/.config/needle/config.yaml\n23\tworker:\n24\t  max_workers: 4              # Maximum concurrent workers (default: 4)\n25\t  idle_timeout: 60            # Seconds to wait between queue polls when idle (default: 60)\n26\t  launch_stagger_seconds: 2   # Delay between worker launches (default: 2)\n27\t```\n28\t\n29\t### Worker Binary Path Override\n30\t\n31\t**When to use this:** Set `worker_binary_path` when the running binary's path is deliberately not what should be spawned as workers. This is needed in these cases:\n32\t\n33\t- **Wrapper script deployments:** If you run NEEDLE via a wrapper script (e.g., for environment setup or signal handling), the supervisor would spawn workers that re-execute the wrapper instead of the actual needle binary.\n34\t- **PATH conflicts:** If another tool on your system is named `needle` and appears earlier in `$PATH`, workers would spawn the wrong binary without this override.\n35\t- **Custom install locations:** If needle is installed at a non-standard path and you want to explicitly control which binary is spawned.\n36\t\n37\t**Default behavior:** When `worker_binary_path` is not set (or `null`), the supervisor resolves the worker binary via `std::env::current_exe()` — this is always correct when supervisor and workers are built from the same binary.\n38\t\n39\t**Example:**\n40\t\n41\t```yaml\n42\t# ~/.config/needle/config.yaml\n43\tworker:\n44\t  # Explicit path to the worker binary\n45\t  # Use absolute paths or paths starting with ~ (expanded to $HOME)\n46\t  worker_binary_path: /opt/needle/bin/needle\n47\t\n48\t  # Or use tilde expansion for home directory\n49\t  # worker_binary_path: ~/local/bin/needle\n50\t```\n51\t\n52\t**How it works:**\n53\t\n54\t- The supervisor logs the resolved binary path at startup (check your logs for \"worker spawn path resolved to...\")\n55\t- The path is validated for existence at startup — a typo or missing binary will fail immediately, not silently spawn the wrong process\n56\t- Relative paths are resolved relative to the supervisor's current working directory\n57\t\n58\t**Troubleshooting:**\n59\t\n60\t```bash\n61\t# Check what binary your supervisor will spawn\n62\tneedle supervise --dry-run\n63\t\n64\t# Verify the path exists and is executable\n65\ttest -x /opt/needle/bin/needle && echo \"OK\" || echo \"MISSING\"\n66\t\n67\t# Check supervisor logs for the resolved path\n68\tgrep \"worker spawn path\" ~/.needle/logs/supervisor.log\n69\t```\n70\t\n71\t**See also:** GitHub issue [jedarden/NEEDLE#11](https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/issues/11) — background on why this override exists.\n72\t\n73\t---\n74\t\n75\t## Agent Configuration\n76\t\n77\tThe `agent` section controls how NEEDLE invokes AI agents.\n78\t\n79\t```yaml\n80\t# ~/.config/needle/config.yaml\n81\tagent:\n82\t  default: claude              # Default agent CLI (default: \"claude\")\n83\t  timeout: 3600                # Agent process timeout in seconds (default: 3600 = 1 hour)\n84\t  args: []                      # Extra arguments passed before the prompt (default: [])\n85\t\n86\t  # Directory containing adapter TOML files (default: ~/.config/needle/adapters)\n87\t  adapters_dir: ~/.config/needle/adapters\n88\t\n89\t  # Model-to-adapter routing (optional)\n90\t  routing:\n91\t    # Rules are evaluated in order; first match wins\n92\t    rules:\n93\t      - match_model: \"(claude-)?(sonnet|opus|fable|haiku).*\"\n94\t        adapter: claude-print    # Use subscription billing for Anthropic models\n95\t    default_adapter: claude-code-glm-4.7  # Fallback for non-matching models\n96\t    strict: false                # If true, fail when no rule matches (default: false)\n97\t```\n98\t\n99\t---\n100\t\n101\t## Workspace Configuration\n102\t\n103\tThe `workspace` section defines where NEEDLE stores state and which workspace to process.\n104\t\n105\t```yaml\n106\t# ~/.config/needle/config.yaml\n107\tworkspace:\n108\t  # Default workspace directory (default: current directory)\n109\t  default: ~/dev/my-project\n110\t\n111\t  # NEEDLE home directory for heartbeats and logs (default: ~/.needle)\n112\t  home: ~/.needle\n113\t\n114\t  # Domain labels for cross-workspace skill sharing (optional)\n115\t  labels:\n116\t    - rust\n117\t    - trading\n118\t    - api\n119\t```\n120\t\n121\t**Workspace overrides (`.needle.yaml`):**\n122\t\n123\tOnly certain fields can be overridden at the workspace level. Every workspace\n124\twith a bead store must explicitly bind its backend; NEEDLE does not infer store\n125\townership from whichever executable appears first on `PATH`.\n126\t\n127\t```yaml\n128\t# .needle.yaml (in workspace root)\n129\tworkspace:\n130\t  labels:                    # ONLY this field is overridable at workspace level\n131\t    - frontend\n132\t    - react\n133\t\n134\tbead_cli:\n135\t  backend: bead-forge       # Existing bead-forge workspace\n136\t# backend: bead-rs          # Native bead-rs workspace after rehydration\n137\t# explicit_path: /opt/bin/bead  # Optional host-specific operator override\n138\t\n139\t# These fields are ignored if set in .needle.yaml:\n140\t# - workspace.default (resolved globally)\n141\t# - workspace.home (resolved globally)\n142\t```\n143\t\n144\t`bead-forge` resolves the `bf` executable and requires its identity to begin\n145\twith `bf `. `bead-rs` resolves `bead` and requires `bead `. Identity is checked\n146\tbefore the store is opened. A missing, unknown, or mismatched binding makes the\n147\tworkspace ineligible for dispatch. Changing this value does not migrate data:\n148\tinitialize and reconcile the destination store first, then change the binding\n149\tduring the reviewed cutover.\n150\t\n151\tExplore, Splice, and the supervisor load each target repository's binding\n152\tindependently, so bead-forge and bead-rs workspaces can coexist during rollout.\n153\t\n154\t---\n155\t\n156\t## Strand Configuration\n157\t\n158\tNEEDLE runs multiple \"strands\" that find or create work when the primary workspace is empty.\n159\t\n160\t### Explore (Multi-workspace Discovery)\n161\t\n162\t```yaml\n163\t# ~/.config/needle/config.yaml\n164\tstrands:\n165\t  explore:\n166\t    enabled: true                          # Enable Explore strand (default: true)\n167\t\n168\t    # Leave empty for auto-discovery (recommended default)\n169\t    # All directories under workspace_root containing .beads/ are scanned\n170\t    workspaces: []\n171\t\n172\t    # Root for auto-discovery (default: $HOME)\n173\t    workspace_root: ~/dev\n174\t\n175\t    # Minimum cycles between scans; empty scans back off geometrically (default: 1)\n176\t    scan_interval_cycles: 1\n177\t\n178\t    # Maximum cycles between scans after backoff (default: 8)\n179\t    max_scan_interval_cycles: 8\n180\t\n181\t    # Re-scan for new workspaces every N cycles (default: 60)\n182\t    rediscovery_cycles: 60\n183\t\n184\t    # Alert if no beads claimed for this many minutes (default: 15)\n185\t    starvation_threshold_minutes: 15\n186\t```\n187\t\n188\t**Pinned mode (exception):** To restrict a worker to specific workspaces:\n189\t\n190\t```yaml\n191\tstrands:\n192\t  explore:\n193\t    workspaces:\n194\t      - ~/dev/project-a\n195\t      - ~/dev/project-b\n196\t    # WARNING: When workspaces is non-empty, auto-discovery is DISABLED\n197\t    # and only the listed paths are scanned\n198\t```\n199\t\n200\t### Mitosis (Bead Splitting)\n201\t\n202\t```yaml\n203\tstrands:\n204\t  mitosis:\n205\t    enabled: true                # Enable mitosis (default: true)\n206\t    first_failure_only: true     # Only split on first failure (default: true)\n207\t    force_failure_threshold: 0  # Force split after N failures (0 = disabled)\n208\t    repeat_interval: 0           # Re-split every N failures (0 = disabled)\n209\t    max_depth: 0                # Maximum generation depth (0 = unlimited)\n210\t\n211\t    # Timeout-triggered mitosis (opt-in, default: disabled)\n212\t    timeout_triggered:\n213\t      enabled: false\n214\t      agent_wallclock_timeout: false\n215\t      handler_timeout: false\n216\t      min_elapsed_fraction: 0.9  # Trigger only if 90% of timeout elapsed\n217\t```\n218\t\n219\t### Weave, Unravel, Pulse (Opt-in Strands)\n220\t\n221\tThese strands are disabled by default — enable them explicitly:\n222\t\n223\t```yaml\n224\tstrands:\n225\t  weave:\n226\t    enabled: false              # Opt-in (default: false)\n227\t    max_beads_per_run: 5       # Maximum beads to create per run\n228\t    cooldown_hours: 24          # Minimum hours between runs\n229\t    doc_patterns:\n230\t      - \"README*\"\n231\t      - \"AGENTS.md\"\n232\t      - \"docs/**/*\"\n233\t\n234\t  unravel:\n235\t    enabled: false              # Opt-in (default: false)\n236\t    max_beads_per_run: 5\n237\t    max_alternatives_per_bead: 3\n238\t    cooldown_hours: 168        # 7 days\n239\t\n240\t  pulse:\n241\t    enabled: false              # Opt-in (default: false)\n242\t    max_beads_per_run: 5\n243\t    cooldown_hours: 48\n244\t    severity_threshold: 3      # 1-5, where 1 is critical\n245\t    scanners:\n246\t      - name: clippy\n247\t        command: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings\n248\t```\n249\t\n250\t---\n251\t\n252\t## Telemetry Configuration\n253\t\n254\tNEEDLE emits structured telemetry (logs, metrics, traces) to multiple sinks.\n255\t\n256\t### File Sink (Local Logs)\n257\t\n258\t```yaml\n259\ttelemetry:\n260\t  file_sink:\n261\t    enabled: true               # Write logs to files (default: true)\n262\t    log_dir: null               # Null = use workspace.home/logs\n263\t    retention_days: 30          # Delete logs older than this (default: 30)\n264\t```\n265\t\n266\t### Stdout Sink (Console Output)\n267\t\n268\t```yaml\n269\ttelemetry:\n270\t  stdout_sink:\n271\t    enabled: false               # Print to stdout (default: false)\n272\t    format: normal               # minimal | normal | verbose (default: normal)\n273\t    color: auto                 # auto | always | never (default: auto)\n274\t```\n275\t\n276\t### OTLP Sink (OpenTelemetry Export)\n277\t\n278\t```yaml\n279\ttelemetry:\n280\t  otlp_sink:\n281\t    enabled: false               # Export to OTLP collector (default: false)\n282\t    endpoint: \"http://localhost:4317\"  # gRPC endpoint\n283\t    protocol: \"grpc\"            # grpc | http\n284\t    timeout_secs: 10            # Request timeout (default: 10)\n285\t    compression: \"gzip\"          # Path to custom CA certificate (empty = system trust store)\n289\t    headers: []                 # e.g. [\"Authorization: env:NEEDLE_OTLP_AUTHORIZATION\"]\n290\t    resource_attributes: []     # Format: \"key=value\"\n291\t    metrics_interval_secs: 10   # Metrics export interval (default: 10)\n292\t    service_namespace: \"needle-fleet\"\n293\t```\n294\t\n295\tThe mapping above is the canonical representation in v0.3.1 and later. For\n296\tupgrade compatibility, legacy `tls: none` and `tls: tls` values are still\n297\taccepted and normalize to `{insecure: true, ca_file: \"\"}` and\n298\t`{insecure: false, ca_file: \"\"}` respectively. Convert those values to the\n299\tmapping above when editing a config; unsupported values such as `mtls` produce\n300\ta validation error before the worker starts.\n301\t\n302\tIf the collector requires authorization, keep the secret out of YAML and use\n303\tan environment reference in `headers`, for example\n304\t`Authorization: env:NEEDLE_OTLP_AUTHORIZATION`. NEEDLE Configuration Guide\n\nNEEDLE reads configuration from multiple sources in order of precedence (highest last):\n\n1. Built-in defaults\n2. Global config file (`~/.config/needle/config.yaml`)\n3. Workspace config file (`.needle.yaml` in workspace root)\n4. Environment variables (`NEEDLE_*` prefix)\n5. CLI arguments\n\nThis guide covers the most commonly used configuration options.\n\n---\n\n## Worker Configuration\n\nThe `worker` section controls fleet behavior and worker spawning.\n\n### Basic Worker Settings\n\n```yaml\n# ~/.config/needle/config.yaml\nworker:\n  max_workers: 4              # Maximum concurrent workers (default: 4)\n  idle_timeout: 60            # Seconds to wait between queue polls when idle (default: 60)\n  launch_stagger_seconds: 2   # Delay between worker launches (default: 2)\n```\n\n### Worker Binary Path Override\n\n**When to use this:** Set `worker_binary_path` when the running binary's path is deliberately not what should be spawned as workers. This is needed in these cases:\n\n- **Wrapper script deployments:** If you run NEEDLE via a wrapper script (e.g., for environment setup or signal handling), the supervisor would spawn workers that re-execute the wrapper instead of the actual needle binary.\n- **PATH conflicts:** If another tool on your system is named `needle` and appears earlier in `$PATH`, workers would spawn the wrong binary without this override.\n- **Custom install locations:** If needle is installed at a non-standard path and you want to explicitly control which binary is spawned.\n\n**Default behavior:** When `worker_binary_path` is not set (or `null`), the supervisor resolves the worker binary via `std::env::current_exe()` — this is always correct when supervisor and workers are built from the same binary.\n\n**Example:**\n\n```yaml\n# ~/.config/needle/config.yaml\nworker:\n  # Explicit path to the worker binary\n  # Use absolute paths or paths starting with ~ (expanded to $HOME)\n  worker_binary_path: /opt/needle/bin/needle\n\n  # Or use tilde expansion for home directory\n  # worker_binary_path: ~/local/bin/needle\n```\n\n**How it works:**\n\n- The supervisor logs the resolved binary path at startup (check your logs for \"worker spawn path resolved to...\")\n- The path is validated for existence at startup — a typo or missing binary will fail immediately, not silently spawn the wrong process\n- Relative paths are resolved relative to the supervisor's current working directory\n\n**Troubleshooting:**\n\n```bash\n# Check what binary your supervisor will spawn\nneedle supervise --dry-run\n\n# Verify the path exists and is executable\ntest -x /opt/needle/bin/needle && echo \"OK\" || echo \"MISSING\"\n\n# Check supervisor logs for the resolved path\ngrep \"worker spawn path\" ~/.needle/logs/supervisor.log\n```\n\n**See also:** GitHub issue [jedarden/NEEDLE#11](https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/issues/11) — background on why this override exists.\n\n---\n\n## Agent Configuration\n\nThe `agent` section controls how NEEDLE invokes AI agents.\n\n```yaml\n# ~/.config/needle/config.yaml\nagent:\n  default: claude              # Default agent CLI (default: \"claude\")\n  timeout: 3600                # Agent process timeout in seconds (default: 3600 = 1 hour)\n  args: []                      # Extra arguments passed before the prompt (default: [])\n\n  # Directory containing adapter TOML files (default: ~/.config/needle/adapters)\n  adapters_dir: ~/.config/needle/adapters\n\n  # Model-to-adapter routing (optional)\n  routing:\n    # Rules are evaluated in order; first match wins\n    rules:\n      - match_model: \"(claude-)?(sonnet|opus|fable|haiku).*\"\n        adapter: claude-print    # Use subscription billing for Anthropic models\n    default_adapter: claude-code-glm-4.7  # Fallback for non-matching models\n    strict: false                # If true, fail when no rule matches (default: false)\n```\n\n---\n\n## Workspace Configuration\n\nThe `workspace` section defines where NEEDLE stores state and which workspace to process.\n\n```yaml\n# ~/.config/needle/config.yaml\nworkspace:\n  # Default workspace directory (default: current directory)\n  default: ~/dev/my-project\n\n  # NEEDLE home directory for heartbeats and logs (default: ~/.needle)\n  home: ~/.needle\n\n  # Domain labels for cross-workspace skill sharing (optional)\n  labels:\n    - rust\n    - trading\n    - api\n```\n\n**Workspace overrides (`.needle.yaml`):**\n\nOnly certain fields can be overridden at the workspace level. Every workspace\nwith a bead store must explicitly bind its backend; NEEDLE does not infer store\nownership from whichever executable appears first on `PATH`.\n\n```yaml\n# .needle.yaml (in workspace root)\nworkspace:\n  labels:                    # ONLY this field is overridable at workspace level\n    - frontend\n    - react\n\nbead_cli:\n  backend: bead-forge       # Existing bead-forge workspace\n# backend: bead-rs          # Native bead-rs workspace after rehydration\n# explicit_path: /opt/bin/bead  # Optional host-specific operator override\n\n# These fields are ignored if set in .needle.yaml:\n# - workspace.default (resolved globally)\n# - workspace.home (resolved globally)\n```\n\n`bead-forge` resolves the `bf` executable and requires its identity to begin\nwith `bf `. `bead-rs` resolves `bead` and requires `bead `. Identity is checked\nbefore the store is opened. A missing, unknown, or mismatched binding makes the\nworkspace ineligible for dispatch. Changing this value does not migrate data:\ninitialize and reconcile the destination store first, then change the binding\nduring the reviewed cutover.\n\nExplore, Splice, and the supervisor load each target repository's binding\nindependently, so bead-forge and bead-rs workspaces can coexist during rollout.\n\n---\n\n## Strand Configuration\n\nNEEDLE runs multiple \"strands\" that find or create work when the primary workspace is empty.\n\n### Explore (Multi-workspace Discovery)\n\n```yaml\n# ~/.config/needle/config.yaml\nstrands:\n  explore:\n    enabled: true                          # Enable Explore strand (default: true)\n\n    # Leave empty for auto-discovery (recommended default)\n    # All directories under workspace_root containing .beads/ are scanned\n    workspaces: []\n\n    # Root for auto-discovery (default: $HOME)\n    workspace_root: ~/dev\n\n    # Minimum cycles between scans; empty scans back off geometrically (default: 1)\n    scan_interval_cycles: 1\n\n    # Maximum cycles between scans after backoff (default: 8)\n    max_scan_interval_cycles: 8\n\n    # Re-scan for new workspaces every N cycles (default: 60)\n    rediscovery_cycles: 60\n\n    # Alert if no beads claimed for this many minutes (default: 15)\n    starvation_threshold_minutes: 15\n```\n\n**Pinned mode (exception):** To restrict a worker to specific workspaces:\n\n```yaml\nstrands:\n  explore:\n    workspaces:\n      - ~/dev/project-a\n      - ~/dev/project-b\n    # WARNING: When workspaces is non-empty, auto-discovery is DISABLED\n    # and only the listed paths are scanned\n```\n\n### Mitosis (Bead Splitting)\n\n```yaml\nstrands:\n  mitosis:\n    enabled: true                # Enable mitosis (default: true)\n    first_failure_only: true     # Only split on first failure (default: true)\n    force_failure_threshold: 0  # Force split after N failures (0 = disabled)\n    repeat_interval: 0           # Re-split every N failures (0 = disabled)\n    max_depth: 0                # Maximum generation depth (0 = unlimited)\n\n    # Timeout-triggered mitosis (opt-in, default: disabled)\n    timeout_triggered:\n      enabled: false\n      agent_wallclock_timeout: false\n      handler_timeout: false\n      min_elapsed_fraction: 0.9  # Trigger only if 90% of timeout elapsed\n```\n\n### Weave, Unravel, Pulse (Opt-in Strands)\n\nThese strands are disabled by default — enable them explicitly:\n\n```yaml\nstrands:\n  weave:\n    enabled: false              # Opt-in (default: false)\n    max_beads_per_run: 5       # Maximum beads to create per run\n    cooldown_hours: 24          # Minimum hours between runs\n    doc_patterns:\n      - \"README*\"\n      - \"AGENTS.md\"\n      - \"docs/**/*\"\n\n  unravel:\n    enabled: false              # Opt-in (default: false)\n    max_beads_per_run: 5\n    max_alternatives_per_bead: 3\n    cooldown_hours: 168        # 7 days\n\n  pulse:\n    enabled: false              # Opt-in (default: false)\n    max_beads_per_run: 5\n    cooldown_hours: 48\n    severity_threshold: 3      # 1-5, where 1 is critical\n    scanners:\n      - name: clippy\n        command: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings\n```\n\n---\n\n## Telemetry Configuration\n\nNEEDLE emits structured telemetry (logs, metrics, traces) to multiple sinks.\n\n### File Sink (Local Logs)\n\n```yaml\ntelemetry:\n  file_sink:\n    enabled: true               # Write logs to files (default: true)\n    log_dir: null               # Null = use workspace.home/logs\n    retention_days: 30          # Delete logs older than this (default: 30)\n```\n\n### Stdout Sink (Console Output)\n\n```yaml\ntelemetry:\n  stdout_sink:\n    enabled: false               # Print to stdout (default: false)\n    format: normal               # minimal | normal | verbose (default: normal)\n    color: auto                 # auto | always | never (default: auto)\n```\n\n### OTLP Sink (OpenTelemetry Export)\n\n```yaml\ntelemetry:\n  otlp_sink:\n    enabled: false               # Export to OTLP collector (default: false)\n    endpoint: \"http://localhost:4317\"  # gRPC endpoint\n    protocol: \"grpc\"            # grpc | http\n    timeout_secs: 10            # Request timeout (default: 10)\n    compression: \"gzip\"          # gzip | none | zstd\n    tls:                        # Canonical TLS configuration\n      insecure: false           # Disable TLS verification (not recommended for production)\n      ca_file: \"\"               # Path to custom CA certificate (empty = system trust store)\n    headers: []                 # e.g. [\"Authorization: env:NEEDLE_OTLP_AUTHORIZATION\"]\n    resource_attributes: []     # Format: \"key=value\"\n    metrics_interval_secs: 10   # Metrics export interval (default: 10)\n    service_namespace: \"needle-fleet\"\n```\n\nThe mapping above is the canonical representation in v0.3.1 and later. For\nupgrade compatibility, legacy `tls: none` and `tls: tls` values are still\naccepted and normalize to `{insecure: true, ca_file: \"\"}` and\n`{insecure: false, ca_file: \"\"}` respectively. Convert those values to the\nmapping above when editing a config; unsupported values such as `mtls` produce\na validation error before the worker starts.\n\nIf the collector requires authorization, keep the secret out of YAML and use\nan environment reference in `headers`, for example\n`Authorization: env:NEEDLE_OTLP_AUTHORIZATION`. The environment variable must\ncontain the complete header value (such as `Bearer <token>`).\n\n### Webhooks (Hooks)\n\n```yaml\ntelemetry:\n  hooks:\n    - event_filter: \"outcome.*\"         # Glob pattern matched against event_type\n      command: \"/path/to/alert.sh\"      # Shell command (event JSON via stdin)\n      url: \"https://hooks.slack.com/...\"  # Webhook URL (optional)\n```\n\n---\n\n## Health Configuration\n\n```yaml\nhealth:\n  # Heartbeat interval in seconds (default: 30)\n  heartbeat_interval_secs: 30\n\n  # Heartbeat TTL in seconds (default: 300)\n  # Heartbeats older than this are considered stale\n  heartbeat_ttl_secs: 300\n\n  # Directory for heartbeat files (default: state/heartbeats under workspace.home)\n  heartbeat_dir: null\n```\n\n---\n\n## Validation Configuration\n\n```yaml\nvalidation:\n  # Timeout for gate execution in seconds (default: 50)\n  outcome_timeout_seconds: 50\n\n  # Maximum bytes of gate command stderr captured on failure (default: 4096)\n  stderr_cap_bytes: 4096\n```\n\n---\n\n## Supervisor Configuration\n\n```yaml\nsupervisor:\n  # Path to supervisor's heartbeat file\n  # (default: workspace.home/state/supervisor-heartbeat.json)\n  heartbeat_path: null\n\n  # Path to supervisor's control socket (optional)\n  socket_path: null\n```\n\n---\n\n## Environment Variable Overrides\n\nAny config field can be overridden via environment variables with the `NEEDLE_` prefix and `__` as separator:\n\n```bash\n# Set agent default\nexport NEEDLE_AGENT__DEFAULT=claude-interactive\n\n# Set timeout\nexport NEEDLE_AGENT__TIMEOUT=7200\n\n# Set routing\nexport NEEDLE_AGENT__ROUTING__DEFAULT_ADAPTER=claude-print\n\n# Set worker limits\nexport NEEDLE_WORKER__MAX_WORKERS=8\nexport NEEDLE_WORKER__IDLE_TIMEOUT=120\n\n# Set workspace\nexport NEEDLE_WORKSPACE__DEFAULT=~/dev/my-project\n```\n\n---\n\n## Complete Example Configuration\n\n```yaml\n# ~/.config/needle/config.yaml\nworker:\n  max_workers: 4\n  idle_timeout: 60\n  launch_stagger_seconds: 2\n  worker_binary_path: /opt/needle/bin/needle  # Override only if needed\n\nagent:\n  default: claude\n  timeout: 3600\n  adapters_dir: ~/.config/needle/adapters\n  routing:\n    rules:\n      - match_model: \"(claude-)?(sonnet|opus|fable|haiku).*\"\n        adapter: claude-print\n    default_adapter: claude-code-glm-4.7\n    strict: false\n\n# Put this binding in the repository's .needle.yaml, not only global config.\nbead_cli:\n  backend: bead-forge\n\nworkspace:\n  default: ~/dev/my-project\n  home: ~/.needle\n  labels:\n    - rust\n    - api\n\nstrands:\n  pluck:\n    exclude_labels: []\n    split_after_failures: 3\n  explore:\n    enabled: true\n    workspaces: []\n    workspace_root: ~/dev\n    scan_interval_cycles: 1\n    max_scan_interval_cycles: 8\n    rediscovery_cycles: 60\n    starvation_threshold_minutes: 15\n  mitosis:\n    enabled: true\n    first_failure_only: true\n    force_failure_threshold: 0\n    max_depth: 0\n\ntelemetry:\n  file_sink:\n    enabled: true\n    retention_days: 30\n  stdout_sink:\n    enabled: false\n  otlp_sink:\n    enabled: false\n\nhealth:\n  heartbeat_interval_secs: 30\n  heartbeat_ttl_secs: 300\n\nvalidation:\n  outcome_timeout_seconds: 50\n  stderr_cap_bytes: 4096\n```\n\n---\n\n## See Also\n\n- [README.md](../README.md) — Project overview and quickstart\n- [ADR-009](../docs/adr/009-external-adopter-hardening.md) — Background on `worker_binary_path` and validation configurability\n- [Source code: src/config/mod.rs](../src/config/mod.rs) — Full struct definitions and defaults\n","numLines":462,"startLine":1,"totalLines":462}}}
